hook.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
hook.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.

prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

alternates.speaker: King Brihadratha
alternates.setting: The king's plea after listing everything that passes.
alternates.sanskrit: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
alternates.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.
alternates.translation: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
alternates.why: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verse.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
verse.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.for_you: You have built the house and held the title, yet the river of wishing still runs. The water is full, but the banks of worry are high. You can rest on the bank today.
verse.try_today: Notice one wish and name the worry that stands beside it.

why: The river called Hope (Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 10)
Shows worry as part of one river fed by wishing

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Poem 'Hold On Yet a While, Brave Heart', written to the Maharaja of Khetri.
verse.line: Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come.
verse.translation: If the sun by the cloud is hidden a bit, If the welkin shows but gloom, Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come. … Not a work will be lost, no struggle vain, Though hopes be blighted, powers gone; … Then hold on yet a while, brave soul, No good is e'er undone.
verse.why: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

prasang.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

verse.for_you: The house and the title are real. They are not the whole story. No good you have done is undone. The victory is sure to come.
verse.try_today: Notice one small good you did today. Hold on to that fact.

why: no good is ever undone
no struggle is vain

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: You have worked fourteen-hour days for ten years. You have the house and the title, and the feeling remains. The absence of reward does not make the effort worthless.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing today that did not pay off, and let it be only one of two possible endings.
verse.scene_line: Yudhishthira stands beside you, looking at the same empty effort.

why: Weariness at unrewarded work is met by naming both possible ends
Failure is one of two normal outcomes, not a judgement

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verse.line: If even practice is too hard, just do your work for my sake. That alone takes you far.
verse.translation: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for my sake. Even by doing actions for me, you will reach perfection.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.try_today: Do one small task today as an offering to the divine.
verse.scene_line: You stand in a house you built, holding a title that means nothing, waiting for a feeling that will not come.

why: work done for his sake
If you cannot do that, then this

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.for_you: You have built the house and earned the title. Now the mind wanders through the rooms, finding them empty. Rest where you are. Let the day unfold without scripting it.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing that arrives unplanned and let it be enough.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet house and watch the mind wander without a past to replay or a future to script.

why: Enjoying what arrives unplanned
Vishramyatam

story.title: Sampati's burned wings
story.story_hook: The monkeys had given up and were waiting to die when a vulture with no wings spoke to them.
story.summary: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.
story.lesson: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.
story.hook_title: The monkeys had given up and sat down to die, until an old vulture spoke
story.teaser: The monkeys had given up and sat down to die, until an old vulture spoke

The tired 'enough' at the end

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verse.sanskrit: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
verse.line: Everyone suffers from constant straining, and no one notices. Seeing this alone brings peace.
verse.translation: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verse.why: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.
verse.misuse: Not against effort; against the anxious straining that rides on it.

prasang.title: Why striving and study do not bring peace
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra warns that reading scriptures, working or meditating will not bring peace on their own; everyone suffers from straining, and running away from the world doesn't end pain. Even pride in being free is just more suffering.
prasang.lesson: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.

verse.for_you: You have worked hard for years and now the emptiness remains. The house and the title do not fill the space. The quiet truth is that the striving itself was the suffering all along.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind begins to strain after the next thing and let the effort go.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the house you built, and the strain is invisible to you, as it is to everyone.

why: Where craving is, the round is (Ashtavakra Gita 10.3)
names the straining itself as the cause of the misery

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Near the end, Krishna tells Arjuna that a busy, working life is no barrier.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
verse.line: Doing all their work while leaning on me, they reach the lasting home, by my grace.
verse.translation: Even while always doing every kind of work, the one who leans on me reaches the eternal, imperishable home by my grace.

matched.label: I'm burned out and running on empty
Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

verse.for_you: You have built the house, the car, and the title through long days. The work is real, but the feeling of emptiness is also real. You can let the work continue while leaning on the grace that holds the lasting home.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when the work itself feels like a resting place.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the house you built, and the titles you hold, and the work continues around you.

why: daily work is given a destination
the work continues, but it is done leaning on him

verse.speaker: Narada
verse.setting: Narada to Shuka on why more is never enough.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् / तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः
verse.line: There's no end to wanting. Contentment is the highest happiness, and the real wealth.
verse.translation: There is no end to thirst; contentment is the highest happiness. That is why the wise see contentment itself as wealth.
verse.why: Brooding doesn't heal pain, it grows it. Care for the mind as you would the body.

prasang.title: Narada consoles Shuka
prasang.summary: The sage Narada visits the young Shuka and teaches him how to meet sorrow: brooding doubles pain, the mind is healed by understanding as the body by medicine, act if you can fix it, and contentment is the real wealth.
prasang.lesson: Brooding doesn't heal pain, it grows it. Care for the mind as you would the body.

verse.try_today: Notice the wanting without acting on it today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in a house of success and feel the ache of an unquenchable thirst.

why: When the mind is content, who is poor?
No end to wanting is stated flatly

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: How a householder becomes a 'world' for others.
verse.sanskrit: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको
verse.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
verse.translation: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.
verse.for_you: You have the house, the car, the title. You have fed the days. Now let the house feed others. Let your roof become a world for the ones who pass through.
verse.try_today: Give one meal to a person or animal today without expecting anything back.
verse.scene_line: You have built a shelter, and the world is waiting to live inside it.

why: Become a world for others.
feeding and housing others is what makes a home a world

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Having searched all of Lanka without finding Sita, Hanuman fights off despair.
verse.sanskrit: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
verse.line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.
verse.translation: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
verse.why: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

prasang.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
prasang.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.
prasang.story_hook: Hanuman had searched every palace in Lanka by moonlight, and she was nowhere.
prasang.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

verse.for_you: You have built the house and the car, but the title feels hollow. The search is not over. There is still more ground to cover.
verse.try_today: Look again at the room where you have not yet looked.

why: Lakshmana and Hanuman both set the will to go on against despair, inside scenes of real loss.

story.title: Manki's song: desire, I know your root
story.story_hook: Manki put every coin he had into two young oxen, and lost both in a single afternoon.
story.summary: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
story.lesson: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
story.teaser: Manki put every coin he had into two young oxen, and lost both in a single afternoon.
story.for_you: You have the house, the car, and the title. And you feel completely empty. The last ten years were not for this.

queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

plan_v3.first_line: You have the house, the car, the title, and still feel completely empty, so this mind of yours runs here and there for nothing like a stray village dog.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
verse.sanskrit: किं मे राज्येन किं भोगैः कोऽहं किमिदमागतम् । यन्मिथ्यैवास्तु तन्मिथ्या कस्य नाम किमागतम् ॥
verse.line: What is a kingdom to me, or pleasure? Who am I, and what is all this for?
verse.translation: What is kingship to me, and what are pleasures? Who am I, and what is all this that has come to me? If it is unreal, let it be unreal; whose is it, and what has anyone gained?
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
verse.misuse: Rama's question opens the teaching; it isn't the answer. Follow it with 6a.115.43 or 1.30.17.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.for_you: You have the house, the car, the title, and still the day ends in a hollow silence. The title and the house do not fill the space that remains. Rest in the question of who you are before the title.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you do for the title alone today.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verse.sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
verse.line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
verse.translation: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
verse.why: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

prasang.title: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

verse.for_you: You have the title and the car. You also have the restless stirring that never stops. This is what rajas looks like in a life that is full of doing.
verse.try_today: Notice when the next project begins. See the craving that starts it.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
verse.line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
verse.translation: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.for_you: You have the title, the house, the car. The outer life is full. The inner life is quiet. There is a joy in you that does not run out. It is already there.

verse.speaker: Sanatkumara
verse.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verse.line: Happiness is in the vast. There is no happiness in the small.
verse.translation: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

verse.for_you: You have the house and the title, but the small is not enough. The wanting is for the vast. Let that wanting be your guide today.
verse.try_today: Notice the moment the small feels too small and let the vast open there.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the house you have built, and the infinite waits beyond the door.

why: the small always leaves a thirst for more; the wanting is for the vast

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥
verse.line: Money goes one of three ways: given, enjoyed, or lost. Neither give nor enjoy it, and it is lost.
verse.translation: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

verse.scene_line: You sit in the house you built, and the silence asks what was it all for.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha's closing advice to Rama on living in the world after the three vows.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
verse.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
verse.translation: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.for_you: You have the house and the title, but the work has hollowed you out. The sense of being the doer can fall away even while the days are long.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you are acting without clinging to the result.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the house you built while Vasishtha tells Rama to stay turned inward.

why: an inner anchor during activity

story.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
story.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
story.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
